kurz: In a wok you fry small pieces very hot and fast, keeping them moving. Too much at once cools it down, and the vegetables steam instead of frying.
bild_im_kopf: Like a stage with one spotlight: whoever stands in the light gets hot, whoever waits at the edge stays warm.
was_passiert: The thin steel at the bottom gets very hot, the steep sides stay cooler. Tossing brings each piece briefly to the hot base and back to the edge. On a powerful gas burner flames lick over the rim, and vaporising oil droplets give the typical smoky aroma, called wok hei. A home hob lacks this power, so the batch size matters all the more.
warum_wichtig: Most home stir-fries turn watery because too much is in the wok at once. Frying in batches gives browning and bite.
faustregeln: For browning on a home hob: no more than two handfuls per batch, because more pushes the wok below 100 °C.
For crunchy vegetables: add them well dried, because wet vegetables swallow the heat.
Season and care for a carbon steel wok like cast iron.
schritte: Cut and lay out everything beforehand: there is no time once frying starts.
Let the wok get hot until a drop of water dances, only then add oil.
Fry meat and vegetables separately and in small batches, taking each out.
At the end put everything back, add the sauce and toss briefly.
On induction or ceramic hobs, use a wok with a flat base.
